source.title: Learning explanations that are hard to vary
source.authors: Giambattista Parascandolo; Alexander Neitz; Antonio Orvieto; Luigi Gresele; B. Schölkopf

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, though the extracted chess figures and equations contain some formatting noise.
record.tranche_reason: The paper directly tests random-label memorization on CIFAR-10 and reports that its AND-mask prevents convergence on random labels, while standard average gradients memorize them. This refines the claim by showing the outcome depends on the gradient aggregation method.
record.gate_note: CIFAR-10 results test random-label fitting and a 25% label-noise condition. The claim that Zhang et al. (2016) found standard regularizers still permit memorization is cited prior work, not a result of this study. Other experiments on synthetic data and CoinRun do not test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The standard-Adam control repeats the random-label training experiment on CIFAR-10 and reports memorization. The AND-mask experiments change gradient aggregation and therefore fall outside the versions specifying standard training.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the CIFAR-10 conclusion. More broadly, the authors argue that averaging gradients can favor patchwork solutions, formalize invariant learning consistency, and present the AND-mask as one possible implementation. They explicitly acknowledge that it is unlikely to be practical for every application.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares standard gradient averaging with its AND-mask method, which masks gradient components according to sign agreement across examples; it does not reproduce the original random-label experiment as its main method.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome changes with the AND-mask agreement threshold: slightly increasing it quickly hinders memorization on random labels. On original labels the paper reports that the mask did not significantly affect generalization error.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing the AND-mask threshold suppresses random-label memorization; at 25% corruption, masked training resists incorrect targets while test accuracy improves.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing gradient aggregation to require sign agreement can suppress label memorization while preserving useful learning on CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: On the synthetic dataset, standard regularizers favor predictive shortcuts while the AND-mask learns the invariant mechanism.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Standard regularization can fail to select invariant mechanisms when simpler predictive shortcuts are available.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR), 2020; supplied text is marked “Under review. (Preprint)”
record.problems: The CIFAR-10 accuracy outcomes are presented in figures without exact values in the supplied text. Each random-label trial was run twice; the label-noise experiment tested three starting learning rates. The random-label condition does not report test error at chance.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted. Individual threshold-specific plotted values could not be recovered from the supplied text and are represented as figure-only in the notes.

untested.parts: Chance-level test performance under completely random labels cannot be established from the supplied figure extraction; exact final training accuracy is also unavailable.
Relative convergence time for true versus random labels, and slowing across increasing corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect total training fit and steadily increasing test error across a corruption sweep. Only 25% corruption is examined alongside the endpoint experiments.
Random-label fitting under weight decay, dropout and augmentation, and true-label generalization after their removal. The synthetic shortcut experiments measure a different construct.

Direct comparison of when shared real-label patterns and noisy labels are learned. Early test improvement followed by overfitting is suggestive but does not separately establish those learning trajectories.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. AND-mask prevention does not challenge claims restricted to standard training. Figure-specific values are unavailable and their omission is already declared. The supplied manuscript does not substantiate the record's ICLR 2020 publication claim.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests CIFAR-10 with random labels and the original labels, but does not report test error at chance for random labels.

Tests one condition with 25% randomly shuffled training labels, not a sweep from none to all; does not report perfect total training accuracy across corruption fractions or a steadily rising test error.

rows.subject: ResNet (same model as CIFAR-10 memorization experiment)
rows.operation_detail: Trained without AND-mask on CIFAR-10 with 25% of training labels randomly shuffled.
rows.measure: Accuracy on mislabeled training portion and test accuracy
rows.baseline: AND-mask condition on the same 25% label-noise task.
rows.value: “the baseline again memorizes the incorrect labels”; “peaks early then decreases as the model overfits” on the test set
rows.note: The paper states outcomes qualitatively; exact accuracy values are figure-only. This is one noise fraction, not the full sweep in V4.
rows.check: The baseline explicitly memorizes incorrect labels at 25% corruption while initially generalizing. This supports the measured component of V4; total training accuracy and degradation across corruption fractions are not established. Limited coverage alone does not make the measured effect partial.

rows.subject: ResNet (same model as CIFAR-10 memorization experiment)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with AND-mask on CIFAR-10 with 25% of training labels randomly shuffled.
rows.measure: Accuracy on mislabeled training portion and test accuracy
rows.baseline: Without AND-mask, the model memorized the incorrect labels; its test accuracy peaked early then decreased.
rows.value: “performance on the incorrectly labeled portion of the dataset is well below chance”; “the AND-mask slowly but steadily improves” on the test set
rows.note: The paper states outcomes qualitatively; exact accuracy values are figure-only. The reported outcome concerns the mislabeled portion and test set, not total training accuracy.
rows.check: This is a custom mitigation result, with separately selected learning rate and threshold. Below-chance accuracy against incorrect targets reflects resistance to memorization, not reversed generalization or a failure of standard training.
